html:
The Arab conquests were the wars in which Muslim armies from Arabia, after the death of Muhammad in 632, took an empire stretching from Spain to the Indus in a little over a century. They are among the fastest and most lasting conquests in history.

They were led first by the Rashidun and then Umayyad caliphs. The two great powers of the region, the Eastern Roman Empire and the Sasanian Empire of Persia, had just exhausted each other in a long war, and both had been hit by waves of plague.

Main steps:

  • 630s: the Romans lost Syria at the Battle of the Yarmuk in 636. The Persians lost Iraq after the Battle of al-Qadisiyyah.
  • 640s: Egypt fell, and most of Iran. The last Sasanian king died in 651.
  • 670s to 700s: North Africa was taken, against fierce Berber resistance.
  • 711: armies crossed into Spain and also reached Sindh in today's Pakistan.

The expansion stopped at the walls of Constantinople, besieged in vain, and in France at the Battle of Tours in 732. In Central Asia, Muslim armies met China's Tang dynasty at the Battle of Talas in 751, just after the Abbasids took power.

The conquerors did not force conversion. Christians, Jews and Zoroastrians kept their faith but paid a special tax, and most of the population became Muslim only over the following centuries. The conquests joined the Mediterranean, the Middle East and Central Asia into one zone of trade, law and the Arabic language.
